label: Recommendation for investigation - not a confirmed root cause
disclaimer: These are suggestions about where to look and what to measure. Complaint frequency alone does not prove why a problem occurs. Rules were written as general guidance and should be reviewed by someone who knows your business.

rules.title: Credit report data accuracy
rules.context: Consumers say information on their credit report is wrong, for example accounts or balances that are not theirs or are out of date. Complaints usually concern credit reporting companies and the businesses that supply data to them.
recommended_actions: Audit a random sample of disputed records to separate errors in the source data from errors made when records are matched to the right person.
Look for repeat errors tied to the same data suppliers and agree corrections at the source.
Review the rules used to match records to consumers, especially for mixed or merged files.
Confirm what a consumer is told after a dispute, and when.
rules.reason: Wrong-information complaints can come from bad source data, faulty record matching, or slow corrections. An audit shows which applies before any fix is chosen.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if the issue's share is rising meaningfully, or if complaints cluster in one sub-issue such as 'Information is not mine'.
evidence_and_assumptions: Complaint counts show how often people complained, not how often reports are actually wrong.
Assumes the sub-issue field is filled in reliably; it is blank for many records.
follow_up_metrics: Share of disputed records corrected after investigation
Repeat complaints per consumer
Median days to resolve a dispute

rules.title: Handling of credit report disputes

issues: Problem with a credit reporting company's investigation into an existing problem
Problem with a company's investigation into an existing issue

rules.context: Consumers who disputed an item say the investigation was inadequate, slow, or did not change the result.
recommended_actions: Review a sample of closed disputes to check that the consumer's evidence was actually considered.
Measure how many disputes are closed with no change and re-opened by the same consumer.
Check response times against internal targets and look for bottlenecks in the workflow.
Make sure the outcome letter explains the result and next steps in plain language.
rules.reason: Repeated complaints after a dispute suggest the dispute process itself may not be resolving the underlying problem; a case review tests this.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if the issue is rising meaningfully or if negative sentiment is well above the dataset average.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes consumers who complain about the investigation had first filed a dispute.
Sentiment is a rough text-based estimate.
follow_up_metrics: Re-dispute rate
Share of disputes with a documented review of consumer evidence
Days from dispute to outcome letter

rules.title: Access to credit reports and scores

issues: Unable to get credit report/credit score
Unable to get your credit report or credit score

rules.context: Consumers report being unable to obtain their credit report or score, or being charged for them.
recommended_actions: Test the request journey end to end (website, phone, mail) and note where requests fail or stall.
Review identity-verification steps that may be rejecting legitimate requests.
Check that fee and free-access information is clear at the point of request.
rules.reason: Access complaints often point to friction in identity checks or unclear offers, both of which can be reproduced by testing the journey.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if complaints rise sharply or concentrate on a single channel.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes complaints refer to the consumer's own report request.
follow_up_metrics: Request completion rate
Identity-verification failure rate
Complaints per 10,000 requests, if request volumes are available

rules.title: Use of credit reports

issues: Improper use of my credit report

rules.context: Consumers say someone accessed or used their credit report without a valid reason.
recommended_actions: Audit how access reasons are recorded and checked before a report is released.
Review customer-facing explanations of who may view a report and why.
Sample complaints to see whether they concern permission to access, or reporting that followed access.
rules.reason: Without a record of why a report was pulled, neither the business nor the consumer can show that access was justified.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if complaints rise or if many name the same requesting parties.
evidence_and_assumptions: The category mixes several kinds of concern; a sample read is needed to split them.
follow_up_metrics: Share of report pulls with a documented permitted purpose
Complaints per 10,000 report pulls, if available

rules.title: How lenders report accounts to credit bureaus
rules.context: Customers of lenders and card issuers raise concerns about how their account was reported to the credit bureaus, such as wrong status, wrong balances, or reporting that continued after a dispute.
recommended_actions: Compare a sample of reported account details with the lender's own records.
Review how disputes received through the bureaus are answered and how quickly corrections are sent back.
Check how account-status changes (paid, closed, in dispute) reach the reporting system.
rules.reason: Errors in what a lender sends to the bureaus can be found by comparing the data sent with internal records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if complaints mention disputes that were not corrected.
evidence_and_assumptions: The issue name is broad; sub-issues, where present, show the detail.
Assumes the complaint concerns the lender's reports rather than the bureau's handling.
follow_up_metrics: Share of sampled reports that match internal records
Days to send a correction after a confirmed dispute

rules.title: Credit monitoring and identity protection services

issues: Credit monitoring or identity theft protection services
Identity theft protection or other monitoring services
Problem with fraud alerts or security freezes

rules.context: Complaints about paid or free monitoring services, and about placing or lifting fraud alerts and freezes.
recommended_actions: Review sales and enrolment scripts for clarity about cost, cancellation and what the service does not cover.
Check that freezes and alerts are placed and lifted within the promised time.
Look at cancellation and refund handling for subscription products.
rules.reason: Complaints about add-on services often come from expectations set at sale not matching what is delivered; reviewing the sale and cancellation steps tests this.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if complaints mention billing or cancellation, or the share is rising.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes most complaints are about paid services; some may be about free tools.
follow_up_metrics: Cancellation-related complaints per 1,000 subscribers
Time to place or lift a freeze

rules.title: Mortgage hardship, modification and foreclosure
rules.context: Borrowers who are behind or at risk of falling behind report problems getting a modification, being contacted about collection, or facing foreclosure.
recommended_actions: Map the modification process from first request to decision and measure where applications wait or are lost.
Check that borrowers receive consistent information from different staff and that documents are not repeatedly requested.
Review how foreclosure timelines are coordinated with modification reviews.
Track outcomes by servicer or team to see whether problems are concentrated.
rules.reason: A very large complaint share tells us where customers hurt most, but not why. Process mapping and case review are the way to find the reasons.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if the share is rising meaningfully, or if one servicer or sub-issue dominates.
evidence_and_assumptions: This issue was by far the most common in the 2011-2017 data; a falling share can still mean a large absolute volume.
Complaint volume reflects the economic environment as well as service quality.
follow_up_metrics: Median days from modification request to decision
Share of applications needing repeat document requests
Repeat complaints per borrower

rules.title: Mortgage servicing, payments and escrow
rules.context: Borrowers report problems with payment processing, escrow accounts, statements or servicing transfers.
recommended_actions: Audit a sample of payment postings and escrow calculations against source records.
Review the handover process when servicing is transferred between companies.
Check that escrow changes are explained before they affect the payment amount.
rules.reason: Payment and escrow complaints are checkable against records, so an audit can show whether errors exist and where they start.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if the share is rising meaningfully or complaints cluster after servicing transfers.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes the sub-issue field identifies the type of payment problem; it is often blank.
follow_up_metrics: Payment posting error rate in audited samples
Escrow-related complaints per 10,000 loans, if available
Days to correct a posting error

rules.title: Mortgage application and underwriting

issues: Applying for a mortgage or refinancing an existing mortgage

rules.context: Applicants report problems with the application process, broker conduct, or decisions on their application.
recommended_actions: Review the application timeline and the number of times applicants are asked for the same documents.
Check that decision reasons are communicated clearly.
Compare complaint rates across brokers or channels to see whether problems are concentrated.
rules.reason: Origination complaints often arise from communication gaps between applicant, broker and lender; reviewing timelines and requests shows where.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if complaints concentrate in a few channels or rise meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Without application volumes, complaint counts cannot be turned into rates.
follow_up_metrics: Days from application to decision
Share of applications with repeat document requests
Complaints per 1,000 applications, if available

rules.title: Mortgage closing and settlement costs
rules.context: Borrowers report unexpected costs, delays or confusion at closing.
recommended_actions: Compare estimated and final closing costs on a sample of loans and list the line items that change most.
Review when and how estimates are shared with borrowers.
Check how late changes at closing are explained.
rules.reason: Differences between estimates and final costs are measurable and show whether disclosure timing or accuracy is the problem.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if complaints rise or mention specific fee types.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes complaints refer to the closing stage rather than ongoing servicing costs.
follow_up_metrics: Share of loans where final costs exceed estimate
Days between final disclosure and closing

rules.title: Collection attempts on debts the consumer disputes

issues: Cont'd attempts collect debt not owed
Attempts to collect debt not owed

rules.context: Consumers say they are being pursued for a debt that is not theirs, has been paid, or is the wrong amount.
recommended_actions: Review how debt ownership and balances are checked before collection starts.
Check how disputes are logged and whether collection pauses while a dispute is open.
Audit a sample of accounts sold or transferred to confirm the paperwork and balances match.
rules.reason: Complaints of this type suggest records or hand-offs may be incorrect, which an audit of ownership and balance records can confirm or rule out.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if sub-issues such as 'Debt is not mine' or 'Debt was paid' dominate.
evidence_and_assumptions: The sub-issue field is important here and is blank for many records.
A consumer's claim is not proof the debt is not owed.
follow_up_metrics: Share of disputed accounts found to have wrong owner or amount
Collection activity after a dispute was logged
Days to resolve a dispute

rules.title: Debt verification and written notices
rules.context: Consumers say they did not receive, or could not understand, information confirming the debt, or that required notices were missing.
recommended_actions: Check that notices are sent on time and to the right address, using delivery records.
Test notice wording with readers who are not familiar with debt terms.
Review how verification requests are tracked and answered.
rules.reason: Notice problems can be traced through mailing and tracking records, which makes the cause easier to find than for most complaint types.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes complaints concern notices rather than the debt itself.
follow_up_metrics: Share of notices with confirmed delivery
Days to answer a verification request

rules.title: Debt collector contact and communication

issues: Improper contact or sharing of info
Threatened to contact someone or share information improperly

rules.context: Consumers report frequent calls, contact at inconvenient times or places, or sharing of their information with third parties.
recommended_actions: Review call frequency and timing rules and check that systems actually enforce them.
Check that consumer requests to stop or limit contact are recorded and respected.
Review training and call monitoring for how staff talk to third parties.
rules.reason: Contact complaints can be tested against call logs, which show whether policies are followed in practice.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if negative sentiment is far above average.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes call and contact logs are available for review.
Consumers' descriptions of frequency were not verified.
follow_up_metrics: Calls per account per week against policy
Share of do-not-contact requests honoured
Complaints per 1,000 accounts in collection, if available

rules.title: Debt collection statements and threatened actions

issues: Took or threatened to take negative or legal action

rules.context: Consumers say collectors made misleading statements or threatened actions they could not or did not intend to take.
recommended_actions: Review call scripts and letters for statements that could mislead.
Sample call recordings for threats of action that are not backed by a real plan or right.
Involve the compliance team in reviewing the findings.
rules.reason: Statements made to consumers can be sampled and compared with company policy, which shows whether the problem is scripts, training or individual conduct.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if negative sentiment is much higher than average.
evidence_and_assumptions: This is a record of consumer claims, not a finding of wrongdoing.
Whether an action was legally permitted is a question for compliance or legal staff.
follow_up_metrics: Share of sampled calls with a flagged statement
Complaints per 1,000 accounts in collection, if available

rules.title: Delinquent, sold and bankrupt accounts

issues: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account

rules.context: Consumers report problems after falling behind on an account, including being contacted after bankruptcy or after an account was sold.
recommended_actions: Check that account status is updated promptly after bankruptcy filings or account sales.
Review the hand-off of account data when accounts are sold.
Check that collection stops where it should.
rules.reason: Account-status complaints often come from delays in updating records, which can be found by comparing event dates with update dates.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: The category is small and mixed; a sample read is needed.
follow_up_metrics: Days from status-change event to system update
Collection activity after a bankruptcy flag

rules.title: Account opening, closing and management

issues: Managing, opening, or closing your mobile wallet account
Problem getting a card or closing an account

rules.context: Customers report problems opening, closing or managing deposit, card or prepaid accounts, including unexpected closures and holds.
recommended_actions: Review reasons given when accounts are closed or restricted and check they are explained to customers.
Test the closing process and the time to return remaining funds.
Look for common triggers of account restrictions.
rules.reason: Account closure and management complaints often involve unclear reasons or slow fund returns; both can be checked from account records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if complaints mention held funds.
evidence_and_assumptions: The category covers several products; use the product breakdown to see where it concentrates.
follow_up_metrics: Days to return funds after closure
Share of closures with a clear reason given to the customer

rules.title: Deposits, withdrawals and payments

issues: Money was not available when promised

rules.context: Customers report holds on deposits, delays or errors in withdrawals, and payments that did not arrive when expected.
recommended_actions: Review deposit-hold rules and how holds are explained to customers.
Trace a sample of delayed payments through each step to find where time is lost.
Check that availability dates shown to customers match actual availability.
rules.reason: Delays and holds follow set rules and timestamps, so the cause of a delay can usually be traced from system records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes complaints are about the company's processing rather than third-party delays.
follow_up_metrics: Share of deposits made available by the promised date
Median days for payments to complete

rules.title: Overdraft and low-balance problems

issues: Problems caused by my funds being low
Problem caused by your funds being low

rules.context: Customers report overdraft or insufficient-funds charges they did not expect, or other problems when their balance was low.
recommended_actions: Review how and when customers are warned before a charge occurs.
Check the order in which transactions are processed and how this affects the number of fees.
Check that opt-in or opt-out choices are recorded and honoured.
rules.reason: Low-balance complaints often relate to timing and processing order, which can be examined using transaction data.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if fee amounts are frequently mentioned.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes fees are the main concern; sub-issue data is needed to confirm.
follow_up_metrics: Overdraft fees per active account
Share of overdrafts preceded by a customer alert

rules.title: Debit and ATM card use

issues: Using a debit or ATM card

rules.context: Customers report declined cards, ATM problems, or errors when using a debit, ATM or prepaid card.
recommended_actions: Review decline reasons and false-positive rates for fraud controls.
Check ATM and merchant error handling and refund times.
Check how replacement cards are issued and tracked.
rules.reason: Card-use failures can come from fraud controls, network problems or account holds; decline-code data shows which.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or negative sentiment is high.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes decline-reason data is available.
follow_up_metrics: Share of declines later reversed as false alarms
Days to issue a replacement card

rules.title: Fraud, scams and unauthorized transactions

issues: Unauthorized transactions or other transaction problem
Received a loan I didn't apply for
Received a loan you didn't apply for

rules.context: Consumers report transactions or accounts they did not authorize, scams, or loans taken in their name.
recommended_actions: Review how quickly suspicious activity is detected and the customer is told.
Examine how fraud claims are investigated and how consumers are informed of the outcome.
Check how many claims are repeats from the same consumer.
Consider customer-facing scam warnings where scam types are recurring.
rules.reason: Fraud complaints carry direct financial harm. Speed of detection and clarity of the claims process are measurable.
rules.priority_criteria: Treat as higher priority if rising meaningfully, whatever the volume, because each case can mean direct financial loss.
evidence_and_assumptions: Complaints include both fraud against consumers and disputed transactions the consumer actually authorized.
follow_up_metrics: Median days from claim to provisional credit or resolution
Share of claims upheld
Repeat-victim rate

rules.title: Transaction and transfer errors

issues: Problem with a purchase or transfer

rules.context: Consumers report transfers or payments that failed, went to the wrong place, or were for the wrong amount.
recommended_actions: Trace a sample of failed or incorrect transfers through each step.
Check how errors are reported to the customer and how long refunds take.
Review how exchange rates and fees are shown before the customer confirms.
rules.reason: Transaction errors leave records, so the point at which each error entered can be found.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: The category mixes several transaction types; use product breakdown.
follow_up_metrics: Error rate per 10,000 transactions, if volumes are available
Days to correct an error

rules.title: Lender charges to customers' bank accounts

issues: Can't stop charges to bank account
Charged bank acct wrong day or amt
Can't stop withdrawals from your bank account
Money was taken from your bank account on the wrong day or for the wrong amount

rules.context: Borrowers say a lender kept taking money from their bank account, or took the wrong amount or date.
recommended_actions: Check that requests to stop automatic withdrawals are recorded and acted on in time.
Review how payment amounts and dates are set and checked before collection.
Check refund time when a wrong amount is taken.
rules.reason: Whether a stop request was honoured can be checked from the request log against withdrawal dates.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising or if the same borrowers appear repeatedly.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes the sub-issue field and company records are available.
follow_up_metrics: Share of stop requests honoured before the next withdrawal
Days to refund an incorrect withdrawal

rules.title: Billing disputes and statements

issues: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement

rules.context: Cardholders dispute charges, or find statements unclear or incorrect.
recommended_actions: Review the dispute process steps and time limits, and check how outcomes are explained.
Check whether statements make charges, fees and due dates easy to find.
Look at repeated disputes with the same merchants.
rules.reason: Billing complaints can reflect a confusing statement or a slow dispute process; each is checkable.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Disputes may be justified or not; counts alone do not show which.
follow_up_metrics: Days to resolve a dispute
Share of disputes escalated or re-opened

rules.title: Fees and unexpected charges

issues: Charged fees or interest I didn't expect
Charged fees or interest you didn't expect

rules.context: Customers say they were charged fees or interest they did not expect or understand.
recommended_actions: Review how each fee is disclosed before it applies and compare to what customers say they were told.
Check billing records for repeated or duplicate charges.
Review reversal and refund handling for fees.
Look at whether fee-related complaints cluster in particular products.
rules.reason: Unexpected-fee complaints may come from unclear disclosures or billing errors; reading disclosures and checking records distinguishes them.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully or if the same fee type recurs.
evidence_and_assumptions: Counts cannot show whether charges were correct under the agreement.
follow_up_metrics: Fee-related complaints per 10,000 accounts, if available
Share of fee complaints resulting in a reversal

rules.title: Interest rates, credit limits and account terms
rules.context: Customers report disagreements about interest rates, limit changes, or changes in account terms.
recommended_actions: Check that rate and limit changes are notified in clear terms and in time.
Review how balance transfer and cash advance terms are explained.
Check that promotional rates end as customers were told.
rules.reason: Rate and term complaints can be tested by comparing customer notices with account records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes customers had the terms available; the complaint does not show whether they read them.
follow_up_metrics: Share of rate changes with confirmed notice
Complaints per 10,000 accounts, if available

rules.title: Marketing, rewards and product disclosures

issues: Advertising and marketing, including promotional offers
Confusing or misleading advertising or marketing

rules.context: Customers say offers, rewards or product information did not match what they received, or that disclosures were confusing or missing.
recommended_actions: Compare marketing wording and offer terms with what customers actually receive.
Check the rewards process for how points are earned, changed and redeemed.
Test disclosures with readers who do not work in finance.
rules.reason: Marketing and rewards complaints reflect gaps between promise and delivery, which can be checked by comparing the promise with customer records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes the complaint is about the company's own marketing and not a third party's.
follow_up_metrics: Share of rewards claims fulfilled as described
Complaints per 10,000 accounts, if available

rules.title: Add-on and protection products

issues: Problem with additional add-on products or services

rules.context: Customers dispute add-on products, such as debt protection, that they did not know they had or could not cancel.
recommended_actions: Review how add-ons are offered and whether customers clearly agree to them.
Test the cancellation and refund steps.
Check claim handling for protection products.
rules.reason: Add-on complaints often point to unclear consent or hard cancellation, both of which can be checked in enrolment records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: The category is small and may mix several products.
follow_up_metrics: Share of enrolments with recorded consent
Days to cancel and refund

rules.title: Getting a loan or credit and credit decisions

issues: Shopping for a loan or lease
Shopping for a line of credit
Taking out the loan or lease
Applied for loan/did not receive money
Was approved for a loan, but didn't receive money

rules.context: Applicants report problems getting or comparing credit, delays, unclear decisions, or approved funds that did not arrive.
recommended_actions: Review the application timeline and where requests wait.
Check that decisions are explained and that applicants know what to do next.
Trace cases where an approved loan did not pay out.
rules.reason: Origination complaints are tied to specific steps that can be timed and traced.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Without application volumes, counts cannot become rates.
follow_up_metrics: Days from application to decision
Share of approved loans paid out on time

rules.title: Loan account management, payments and payoff

issues: Problem with the payoff process at the end of the loan
Problems at the end of the loan or lease
Loan payment wasn't credited to your account

rules.context: Borrowers report problems with payments not credited, loan balances, payoff amounts, and closing out a loan.
recommended_actions: Audit a sample of payments for posting delays or misapplied amounts.
Check payoff statements for accuracy and timeliness.
Review how liens or titles are released after payoff.
rules.reason: Payment posting and payoff figures can be audited against records.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Assumes records are available for audit.
follow_up_metrics: Payment posting error rate
Days from payoff to lien or title release

rules.title: Repayment difficulty and hardship options

issues: Problems when you are unable to pay

rules.context: Borrowers who are struggling to pay report difficulty finding or getting hardship options, or poor communication when they ask for help.
recommended_actions: Review how easily borrowers can find and request hardship options.
Check consistency of advice given by different staff.
Check how long it takes to get a decision on a request.
rules.reason: Hardship complaints depend on how well help options are communicated and processed; both can be measured.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully, because it may signal customers in financial difficulty.
evidence_and_assumptions: The rise may reflect economic conditions as well as service.
follow_up_metrics: Share of hardship requests answered within target
Share of borrowers entering a plan who stay current

rules.title: Dealing with student loan servicers

issues: Dealing with my lender or servicer
Dealing with your lender or servicer

rules.context: Borrowers report poor service, confusing repayment information or errors in dealings with a loan servicer.
recommended_actions: Sample contacts to find the most common questions that are not resolved on first contact.
Check how repayment plan information is communicated and when plan changes take effect.
Review how records are handled when servicing is transferred.
rules.reason: Servicer-dealing complaints can come from information gaps or process errors; reviewing contacts shows which.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: The rise in this issue may in part come from category renaming; check name variants.
follow_up_metrics: First-contact resolution rate
Repeat contacts per borrower

rules.title: Vehicle repossession and property handling

issues: Lender repossessed or sold the vehicle
Vehicle was repossessed or sold the vehicle

rules.context: Borrowers report repossession, sale or damage of vehicles or property by the lender.
recommended_actions: Review repossession notices and how they are delivered.
Check how personal items and vehicle condition are documented.
Review how sale proceeds and any remaining balance are explained.
rules.reason: Documentation of notices, condition and sales shows whether the process was followed.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising or if damage claims recur.
evidence_and_assumptions: Counts are small.
follow_up_metrics: Share of repossessions with confirmed notice
Damage claims per 100 repossessions

rules.title: Customer service and reaching the company
rules.context: Customers report difficulty reaching the company or poor service when they do.
recommended_actions: Review call wait times, call drop rates and the availability of channels.
Check how many contacts are needed to resolve a problem.
Review training and escalation routes for complex cases.
rules.reason: Service complaints often reflect access and first-contact resolution, both measurable from contact-centre data.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising meaningfully.
evidence_and_assumptions: Complaints about service often sit alongside another issue; read in context.
follow_up_metrics: Average wait time
First-contact resolution rate
Contacts per resolved case

rules.title: Privacy and handling of personal information
rules.context: Consumers raise concerns about how their personal information is stored, used or shared.
recommended_actions: Review who has access to customer information and how access is logged.
Check how privacy notices are communicated.
Review how privacy complaints are routed and answered.
rules.reason: Privacy concerns are best investigated through access logs and policies.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if rising or if complaints mention a possible data exposure.
evidence_and_assumptions: Counts are small; a sample read may show the real concern.
follow_up_metrics: Privacy complaints answered within target
Share of access events with a logged reason

rules.title: Uncategorised complaints ('Other')
rules.context: Complaints filed under 'Other' do not fit a standard category, so their real topics are hidden.
recommended_actions: Read a random sample to find recurring themes that need a new category.
Use text classification on narratives to suggest categories, then check them by hand.
Review the intake form to see whether the options are confusing.
rules.reason: A large 'Other' share hides real topics. Sampling and recategorising turns it into actionable issues.
rules.priority_criteria: Raise priority if its share is large or growing, since it hides what customers are complaining about.
evidence_and_assumptions: Only complaints with narratives can be read; the rest cannot be recategorised.
follow_up_metrics: Share of complaints in 'Other'
Share of sampled 'Other' complaints that fit an existing category
